caption_en:
One country started at 38. The finish is the part nobody guesses.

Babies who die before their first birthday, per 1,000 live births (World Bank, 2024):
Israel 2.7
UAE 3.8
UK 4.1
Saudi Arabia 4.7
USA 5.5
Turkey 8.0
Iran 10.3
Jordan 12.0
Lebanon 15.3
Syria 17.7
Egypt 20.8

In 1960: Israel 38.4, UK 22.9, Lebanon 65.5, Jordan 111, Egypt 173, Turkey 178 (Iran and Saudi Arabia: no data before the 1970s).
Turkey cut its rate by 95%. Lebanon rose from 11.3 (2015) to 15.3 (2024) during its economic crisis. Every country here is far better than in 1960.

Source: World Bank, World Development Indicators, SP.DYN.IMRT.IN (UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation), 1960 to 2024. Modelled estimates; the animation interpolates between years.
Photos: Hadassah Ein Kerem (Davidi Vardi, PikiWiki, CC BY 2.5), Istanbul (SegLig, CC BY 4.0), Riyadh (B.alotaby, CC BY-SA 4.0), Beirut (Wusel007, CC BY-SA 3.0), via Wikimedia Commons.
Made with AI tools. AI voice (Noam's own cloned voice).
caption_he: ב 1960, 38 מכל 1,000 תינוקות בישראל לא הגיעו ליום ההולדת הראשון. היום: 2.7, הנמוך ביותר בטבלה, לפני בריטניה (4.1) וארה"ב (5.5). מקור: הבנק העולמי, 2024.

sources.label: World Bank (UN IGME), infant mortality SP.DYN.IMRT.IN

lines.line: Thirty eight babies in every thousand died before their first birthday. That was Israel in 1960.
Britain was at twenty three. Egypt and Turkey, more than one baby in six.
Then the whole region starts racing down. Israel too: under ten by 1990.
Turkey cuts its rate by ninety five percent.
Egypt falls from one seventy three to twenty one. Iran, from eighty eight to ten.
Lebanon goes the other way. Since 2015, its crisis pushes the rate back up.
Saudi Arabia and the UAE drop below five.
America ends at five and a half. Britain at four point one.
Which number surprised you most? Tell me in the comments.
Two point seven. Fourteen times lower than in 1960.
